source_policy: SEER Cancer Stat Facts, ACS Cancer Facts & Figures 2026, USPSTF. Citable; refresh yearly. NCCN not used.

incidence.lifetime_risk: ~1 in 16 overall (varies sharply with smoking history)
incidence.rank_among_cancers: 3rd most common cancer diagnosis; ~10.8% of new cancer cases
incidence.trend: Incidence falling ~1.9% per year (2014-2023), tracking declining tobacco use

mortality.us_annual_deaths: ~124,990 projected for 2026 — the leading cause of cancer death
mortality.mortality_rate: declining ~4.1% per year (2015-2024), the fastest drop among major cancers
mortality.trend: Survival improving with low-dose CT screening, better staging, and targeted/immuno therapy; metastatic survival rose from ~2% to ~10%

risk_factors.detail: The dominant cause; risk scales with pack-years; secondhand smoke also contributes
Asbestos, diesel exhaust, arsenic, certain metals
COPD, pulmonary fibrosis; first-degree family history
A meaningful minority (often EGFR/ALK-driven adenocarcinoma), more common in women and East Asian ancestry

screening.guideline_summary: USPSTF recommends annual LDCT for adults 50-80 with a 20 pack-year history who currently smoke or quit within 15 years. Cite USPSTF; NCCN not used.
screening.notes: Screening uptake remains low relative to eligibility; eligibility criteria have broadened over time

epidemiology.presentation: Frequently advanced at diagnosis; cough, hemoptysis, dyspnea, chest pain, weight loss, or incidental imaging finding

acs_ff_2026.title: Cancer statistics, 2026

verification_status: VERIFIED against SEER Cancer Stat Facts (2026 release) and ACS Cancer Facts & Figures 2026 via live search on build date; pathologist should still confirm before publication. Stats are the fastest-aging content — refresh yearly.
